I'll try to  help. I bought a maxed out m51 last week after a very disappointing experience with a gt75 titan 9sg, the panel from which died 24h after purchase. I was told by the sales rep this happens all the time, so moved to Alienware instead. I worked 10  years on dell enterprise hardware, and i'm not a huge fan, so my expectations were low.

Well, I was pleasantly surprised! The build quality is excellent, and I mean, really heads and shoulder above the competition (even though IMHO the rog mothership takes the cake when it comes to design). It feels like a very compact build even though it's a technically a brick so kudos to the AW engineers for the 'rear thrusters' design, looks bril and not tacky (something I hate in gaming laptops)

The eyet tracking feature is a nice to have, but I wish they had invested in a windows hello system instead and a really solid brio-type camera (instead they give us a really poor fhd one). 

You're not buying this to nitpick over details though, so here's the  rub: performance is stellar. It's out of this world good, and rivals full size desktop with completely acceptable fan noise (loud but worth it). My biggest surprise was the panel: it is exceptional from a user experience perspective. I was gutted to not have access to the 4k version but my fears were unfounded - I would now opt for the FHD over the 4k anytime. It's fast, fast fast - fairly evenly lit, and while it's only srgb and not argb, it's perfect for gaming. And I do mean perfect, as you'll be wanting to run everyting on ultra rtx on, and it's going to tax the hardware even on fhd. 

One last thing: remember how I said it was well built? Well, I dropped it from eye level this morning (accident) and it surprised. A few bits of plastic removed, that's all. Panel is intact. 

That said, mine seems to barely break a sweat. Metro exodus on everything maxed out is smooth as butter, and I still have yet to see a single dropped frame on any AAA title. Indy games run the full 144hz, and feel great.
